facts.note: Watch showed twenty minutes to nine when the temple struck nine; the uncle made a scene about it in front of everyone.
Went up to the library and stayed there alone; at the temple's ten, watch showed twenty to ten.
At eighteen past ten by his watch, a thump above in the atelier, then the repeater: ten slow deep notes counted, then doubled notes, then quick high ones not counted.
At a quarter past ten someone went quickly up past the library door; at twenty-one past ten someone came quickly down; he did not see who, and the door was shut.
Aunt's piano was playing downstairs when the thump came.

The time (10:32 by his watch), the arrival in the library, and sitting together until eleven all match. But the transcript's 'He' is never identified as Bastien Girard; the context (money owed, 'my uncle knew... said so at dinner') makes the arrival the uncle, not Girard. The person is altered.

added.quote: When the temple struck nine we all had to put our watches on the cloth, and he went round the table telling each of us what was wrong with ours.
added.why: At nine by the temple, everyone's watches were laid out and compared, and the uncle went round checking them, so the dinner watches were being judged against a common reference at that moment.
